thm:3: surjectivity of the induced morphism
nodes.statement: Assumptions A:1 and A:3 hold. Then the induced morphisms $\tau_F(f)$ from Theorem thm:1 are surjective.

nodes.name: thm:4: compositionality
nodes.statement:
Suppose Assumptions A:1 A:4 and A:5 hold. Then there is a functor 
	
	\[ \iota(\mathcal{X}) \xrightarrow{\tau} \text{LeftSlice} \left(  \mathcal{X}  \right) , \]
	
	which maps an arrow $\iota \Omega \xrightarrow{F} \iota \Omega'$ into $\left[ \mathcal{X} \;;\; \Omega \right] \xrightarrow{\tau_F} \left[ \mathcal{X} \;;\; \Omega' \right]$.

nodes.name: A:1: Assumption
nodes.statement: There are complete categories $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$, with initial objects $0_{\mathcal{X}}$ and $0_{\mathcal{Y}}$ respectively, and there is a continuous functor $\iota : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Y}$ such that $0_{\mathcal{Y}} = \iota \left(  0_{\mathcal{X}}  \right)$, and $\iota$ is injective on objects.

nodes.name: A:2: Assumption
nodes.statement: The category $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ from (1) are complete, the functor $\beta$ is continuous. Categories $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{C}$ have initial elements $0_{\mathcal{A}}$ and $0_{\mathcal{C}}$ respectively, and $\alpha \left( 0_{\mathcal{A}} \right) = 0_{\mathcal{C}}$

nodes.name: A:3: Assumption
nodes.statement: For every monomorphism $f$ in $\mathcal{Y}$, there are morphisms $g$ in $\mathcal{Y}$ and $h$ in $\mathcal{Y}$ such that $f = (\iota h) g$.

nodes.name: A:4: Assumption
nodes.statement: The image under $\iota$ of every morphism in $\mathcal{X}$ is injective in $\mathcal{Y}$.

nodes.name: A:5: Assumption
nodes.statement: Any morphism in $\mathcal{Y}$ which is both surjective and injective is an isomorphism.

lem:frgt_adjnt
nodes.statement:
Consider an arrangement of categories and functors $\mathcal{P} \xrightarrow{P} \mathcal{R} \xleftarrow{Q} \mathcal{Q}$. If $\mathcal{P}$ and $\mathcal{Q}$ have initial elements $0_{\mathcal{P}}$ and $1_{\mathcal{Q}}$ respectively, and $P \left( 0_{\mathcal{P}} \right) = 0_{\mathcal{R}}$, then the functor $\mathrm{Frgt}_2 : \left[ P \;;\; Q \right]$ has a left adjoint given by
	
	\[ \left(  \mathrm{Frgt}_2  \right)^{(L)} : \mathcal{Q} \to \left[ P \;;\; Q \right], \quad q \mapsto \; \begin{tikzcd} P 0_{\mathcal{P}} = 0_{\mathcal{R}} \arrow[d, "!_{Qq}"] \\ Qq \end{tikzcd} \]
	
	In fact, $\left(  \mathrm{Frgt}_1  \right)^{(L)}$ is a right inverse of $\mathrm{Frgt}_1$, i.e., $\mathrm{Frgt}_2 \circ \left(  \mathrm{Frgt}_2  \right)^{(L)} = \mathrm{Id}_{\mathcal{Q}}$.

nodes.name: lem:LimPre:extend
nodes.statement:
Given an arrangement of functors 
	
	\[\begin{tikzcd}
		\mathcal{R} & \mathcal{P} \arrow[r, "Q"] \arrow[l, "R"'] & \mathcal{Q} \arrow[r, "F"] & \mathcal{Q}'
	\end{tikzcd}\]
	
	in which $F$ is limit preserving, the following commutation holds between the $\mathrm{LimPre}$ functors :
	
	\[\begin{tikzcd}
		\mathcal{P} \arrow[rrr, bend left=30, "F\circ Q"] \arrow[rr, "Q"'] \arrow[d, "R"'] && \mathcal{Q} \arrow[r, "F"'] & \mathcal{Q}' \\
		\mathcal{R} \arrow[rrr, bend right=30, "\mathrm{LimPre}_{R,F\circ Q}"'] \arrow[rr, "\mathrm{LimPre}_{R,Q}"] && \mathcal{Q} \arrow[r, "F"] & \mathcal{Q}'
	\end{tikzcd}\]
